summary: The skill registry assigns an owner, source, digest and applicability predicate. The delivery-channel registry separately records how that class reaches consumers: delivered, provider-scoped, withheld or a gap. A declaration or published owner package alone does not prove receiver materialization; provider-scoped template payloads are not universal delivery. Kit materialization replaces the former byte-copy synchronization boundary, while Drivers and component-owned packages have their own transport and adoption. Atlas is staged as a driver in source; that does not establish publication or installation in existing consumers, including framework repositories that receive only Kit. Atlas is the primary curated knowledge archive and retrieval path; implementation, accepted decisions, registry declarations and live operational facts retain their own authority. Memory should point to stable record IDs and verification instructions rather than duplicate changing versions, heads or permissions.
title: Declared skill ownership and installed delivery are separate
